* V6–V8 additional VV1–VV5 event prose, variants and codas:
  ChatGPT, with Lorsieab2's canon guidance, character preferences,
  requests for emotional complexity and patcher constraints.

ledger.why: the food and Farming effects on the ending page
designer rule: every ending serves properly prepared breadfruit

grammar_fixes.before: Cook1 wins for flavor; Cook2 accepts
Cook2 wins for texture; Cook1 requests

items.text: roasting brings out the best flavor
the simplest recipe is always the best
a feast should include several seasonings
new ideas are worth trying carefully
The villagers share a warm meal and exchange recipes.
A father enjoys the food while keeping his infant comfortably beside him. He offers a surprisingly sharp critique of the seasoning.
The elder is pleased to see an old recipe remembered, even if the younger cooks have changed it a little.
The children ask for dessert. The cooks announce that the breadfruit WAS dessert. The children look betrayed.
The cooks clean up together, already discussing next year's feast.

intro.name: The breadfruit
intro.text:
The villagers have harvested a quantity of breadfruit. It must be prepared properly before anyone eats it, but the cooks cannot agree on the best method.
(Cook1) insists that {A.1}. (Cook2) argues that {A.2}. An elder claims to remember an old recipe, though the details have become rather fuzzy. A child asks whether they can just eat dessert.

choices.label: Prepare a traditional recipe with the elder's guidance.
Let the cooks compete with properly prepared dishes.
Make a shared meal using several safe preparations.
Ask the children to help plan the presentation.

o1.text: The elder remembers every step, and the meal is delicious.

o2.text: The elder remembers two conflicting versions. The cooks test small batches rather than guessing recklessly.

o3.text: The elder admits that (elder.he/she) always disliked the recipe. Everyone laughs and makes something else.

text_only.reason: an unnamed elder's old opinion, not a game preference

o4.text: The cooks preserve the recipe in the village's records.

c1.text: (Cook1) wins for flavor; (cook2) accepts the result graciously.

c2.text: (Cook2) wins for texture; (cook1) requests a rematch next year.

c3.text: The judges declare a tie, then ask for seconds.

c4.text: The dishes are both safe but so different that the judges decide personal preference cannot settle the argument.

c5.text: The cooks become intensely competitive until an elder reminds them that the village was supposed to be having lunch.

s1.text: The cooks work together and discover a delightful combination.

s2.text: The meal is simple and satisfying. Nobody makes a speech.

s3.text: One cook learns a technique from the other and thanks (othercook.him/her).

s4.text: The cooks agree on every step except the garnish. The argument lasts longer than the cooking.

k1.text: The children arrange the food into a beautiful display.

text_only.reason: narrative: the food is arranged, not gained; the reward is on the ending page (L3171)

k2.text: A child creates a breadfruit sculpture shaped like {@chief}. The resemblance is unfortunate.

k3.text: The children make place cards for everyone, including a frog. The frog does not attend.

k4.text: The cooks appreciate the help, but keep the children away from hot equipment and sharp tools.
